# Vendored corpus — provenance

Everything under `third-party/elements/` is THIRD-PARTY DATA or EVIDENCE-DERIVED DATA,
not code. It is the content corpus our engine ingests and the ground truth for the
XML grammar.

## testdata/

- **Source**: https://github.com/AuroraLegacy/elements (public)
- **Pinned commit**: `4fc7b24e762599f45d2836f3fc7814658d407315` (HEAD, 2026-07-10)
- **Contents**: core/ (incl. `internal.xml`, `ALE.xml`, players-handbook 2014+2024,
  dungeon-masters-guide, monster-manual), supplements/, unearthed-arcana/,
  collaborations/, index files.
- **Repository policy**: the corpus is NOT committed to git. `npm run corpus:fetch`
  downloads the pinned commit tarball, verifies every file byte-for-byte against the
  committed `testdata.manifest.sha256`, and stages only verified files into
  `testdata/`. The committed `testdata.provenance.json` records the pinned commit and
  accepted file count (796). Coverage gate fails with a hint when the corpus is absent.
- **Licence**: content licensing is recorded upstream per source element; see
  `testdata.provenance.json` and the upstream repo.
- **Redistributed subsets**: the System Reference Document 5.2.1 subset of
  `core/players-handbook-2024/` ships in the browser baseline as
  `apps/client/public/content/srd-5.2.1/`, and the System Reference Document
  5.1 subset of `core/players-handbook/` and
  `core/dungeon-masters-guide/items/` as `apps/client/public/content/srd-5.1/`
  (each plus the Internal elements it grants from `core/internal.xml`). Both
  are generated by `scripts/build-srd-content.mjs` from the reviewed allowlists
  under `third-party/srd-5.2/` and `third-party/srd-5.1/` (see their
  `provenance.md`). Nothing else from `testdata/` is ever bundled.

## The engine's system elements

The system elements the engine supplies itself (element identities, proxies,
unarmed-strike riders, extended identities) are **not** part of this corpus:
they are authored and ship with the client under
`apps/client/public/content/system/`. They are listed here only because the
Node-side library builder combines them with the corpus (see
`packages/engine/src/testing/corpus.ts`).

- `system-elements.xml` — authored from the `.dnd5e` file format itself
  (`<elements>`/`<sum>` nodes carry `type="..." name="..." id="..."` for every
  registered element) and the public `internal.xml` convention (`source="Internal"`).
- `system-elements-extended.xml` — the identities of every element the library
  lacked (levels 9-20, damage types, conditions, armor/weapon groups, supports,
  grants, generated ASI class features, synthesized multiclass variants).
- Proxy elements (`ID_*_INTERNAL_ITEM_*`) are generated at ingest per character
  (naming rule: `Additional {Grant}, {Name}`), never stored.

## ../srd-5.2/

- **What**: the pinned System Reference Document 5.2.1 (PDF sha256 in
  `srd-5.2.1.provenance.json`), the entity inventory extracted from it
  (`srd-5.2.1.inventory.json`, generated by `scripts/extract-srd-inventory.mjs`),
  the reviewed map from that inventory to corpus element ids
  (`srd-5.2.1.map.json`: entries, curated keeps, exclusions, the spell rename
  table and the prose edits), and the name denylist the build enforces
  (`ip-denylist.json`).
- **Licence**: SRD 5.2.1 is published by Wizards of the Coast LLC under
  CC BY 4.0. The shipped notice lives in
  `apps/client/public/legal/index.html`.
- **2014 baseline**: the shipped 2014 files are generated the same way from the
  corpus handbook chapters; see `../srd-5.1/provenance.md`.

## Why testdata + system?

The Node-side element library is built from the public corpus + the shipped system files.
Consistency of the resulting library (counts per element type, element identities,
and behavior) is enforced by the corpus gates and the pinned unit tests.
